question: Assign seven staff members (Person 0 to Person 6) to three projects (Project 0, Project 1, and Project 2) such that each staff member is assigned to exactly one project. Each project has specific skill requirements: Project 0 requires a skill level of 8 for Skill 0 and 8 for Skill 1, Project 1 requires a skill level of 7 for Skill 0 and 9 for Skill 1, and Project 2 requires a skill level of 9 for Skill 0 and 7 for Skill 1. Each staff member has specific skill levels: Person 0 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 1 has Skill 0 level 6 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 2 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 3 has Skill 0 level 6 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 4 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 6, Person 5 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 6, and Person 6 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7. The attained skill level for each project is the sum of the skill levels of the assigned staff members. The skill shortage for each project is the difference between the required skill level and the attained skill level. The goal is to minimize the maximum skill shortage across all projects and skills. Constraints include ensuring that each staff member is assigned to exactly one project, and that the skill shortages for Project 0, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -8, for Project 0, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -8, for Project 1, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -7, for Project 1, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -9, for Project 2, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -9, and for Project 2, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -7.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "persons": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "projects": [0, 1, 2],
    "skills": [0, 1],
    # staff skill levels: skill_level[person][skill]
    "skill_level": {
        0: {0: 5, 1: 7},
        1: {0: 6, 1: 7},
        2: {0: 5, 1: 7},
        3: {0: 6, 1: 7},
        4: {0: 5, 1: 6},
        5: {0: 5, 1: 6},
        6: {0: 5, 1: 7},
    },
    # required skill level: required[project][skill]
    "required": {
        0: {0: 8, 1: 8},
        1: {0: 7, 1: 9},
        2: {0: 9, 1: 7},
    },
    # upper bounds on shortage per (project, skill) from the problem statement
    "shortage_ub": {
        (0, 0): -8,
        (0, 1): -8,
        (1, 0): -7,
        (1, 1): -9,
        (2, 0): -9,
        (2, 1): -7,
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    persons = d["persons"]
    projects = d["projects"]
    skills = d["skills"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=persons)
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=projects)
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=skills)
    model.JS = pyo.Set(initialize=[(j, s) for j in projects for s in skills])

    # assignment variables
    model.assign = pyo.Var(model.P, model.J, within=pyo.Binary)

    # shortage per (project, skill); may be negative
    model.shortage = pyo.Var(model.JS, within=pyo.Reals)

    # maximum shortage (epigraph variable)
    model.maxshort = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # each person assigned to exactly one project
    def assign_once_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.assign[p, j] for j in m.J) == 1

    model.assign_once = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=assign_once_rule)

    # shortage definition
    def shortage_def_rule(m, j, s):
        attained = sum(d["skill_level"][p][s] * m.assign[p, j] for p in m.P)
        return m.shortage[j, s] == d["required"][j][s] - attained

    model.shortage_def = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=shortage_def_rule)

    # shortage upper bounds from the problem text
    def shortage_ub_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.shortage[j, s] <= d["shortage_ub"][(j, s)]

    model.shortage_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=shortage_ub_rule)

    # max linking: maxshort >= every shortage
    def max_link_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.maxshort >= m.shortage[j, s]

    model.max_link = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=max_link_rule)

    # objective: minimise the maximum shortage
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.maxshort, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):

    model.JS = pyo.Set(initialize=[(j, s) for j in d["projects"] for s in d["skills"]])
    model.PJ = pyo.Set(initialize=[(p, j) for p in d["persons"] for j in d["projects"]])

    # x[p,j] = 1 if person p assigned to project j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.PJ, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z = maximum skill shortage across all projects and skills
    model.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(d["z_lb"], None))

    def assign_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.x[p, j] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.assign = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=assign_rule)

    def shortage_ub_rule(m, j, s):
        attained = sum(d["skill_level"][(p, s)] * m.x[p, j] for p in m.P)
        shortage = d["required"][(j, s)] - attained
        return shortage <= d["shortage_ub"][(j, s)]
    model.shortage_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=shortage_ub_rule)

    # Epigraph: z >= shortage for every (project, skill)
    def epigraph_rule(m, j, s):
        attained = sum(d["skill_level"][(p, s)] * m.x[p, j] for p in m.P)
        shortage = d["required"][(j, s)] - attained
        return m.z >= shortage
    model.epigraph = pyo.Constraint(model.JS, rule=epigraph_rule)

    # Minimize the maximum skill shortage
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.z, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.I = pyo.Set(initialize=d["persons"])
    m.J = pyo.Set(initialize=d["projects"])
    m.K = pyo.Set(initialize=d["skills"])

    # x[i,j] = 1 if person i assigned to project j
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.I, m.J, within=pyo.Binary)

    # s[j,k] = shortage for project j, skill k
    m.s = pyo.Var(
        m.J, m.K,
        within=pyo.Reals,
        bounds=(d["shortage_lb"], None),
    )

    # z = max shortage across projects and skills (to minimize)
    m.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Reals, bounds=(d["z_lb"], None))

    # Each person assigned to exactly one project
    def assign_rule(mm, i):
        return sum(mm.x[i, j] for j in mm.J) == 1
    m.assign_con = pyo.Constraint(m.I, rule=assign_rule)

    # Shortage definition: s[j,k] = req[j,k] - sum_i staff[i][k]*x[i,j]
    def shortage_def_rule(mm, j, k):
        return mm.s[j, k] == d["requirement"][j][k] - sum(
            d["staff"][i][k] * mm.x[i, j] for i in mm.I
        )
    m.shortage_def = pyo.Constraint(m.J, m.K, rule=shortage_def_rule)

    # Explicit shortage upper bounds from problem text (<=)
    def shortage_ub_rule(mm, j, k):
        return mm.s[j, k] <= d["shortage_ub"][(j, k)]
    m.shortage_ub_con = pyo.Constraint(m.J, m.K, rule=shortage_ub_rule)

    # Epigraph: z >= s[j,k] for all j,k  (z is at least max shortage)
    def epigraph_rule(mm, j, k):
        return mm.z >= mm.s[j, k]
    m.epigraph = pyo.Constraint(m.J, m.K, rule=epigraph_rule)

    # Minimize the maximum shortage
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.z, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m

    },
    # loose big-M style bounds for T
    "T_lb": -1000.0,
    "T_ub": 1000.0,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    P = d["persons"]
    J = d["projects"]
    S = d["skills"]
    PJ = [(p, j) for p in P for j in J]
    JS = [(j, s) for j in J for s in S]

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.PERSON = pyo.Set(initialize=P)
    m.PROJECT = pyo.Set(initialize=J)
    m.SKILL = pyo.Set(initialize=S)
    m.PJ = pyo.Set(initialize=PJ, dimen=2)
    m.JS = pyo.Set(initialize=JS, dimen=2)

    # Assignment variable: 1 if person p works on project j
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.PJ, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Skill shortage for project j, skill s (required - attained)
    m.u = pyo.Var(m.JS, within=pyo.Reals)

    # Minimax objective variable
    m.T = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Reals,
                  bounds=(d["T_lb"], d["T_ub"]))

    def assign_once_rule(mm, p):
        return sum(mm.x[p, j] for j in mm.PROJECT) == 1
    m.assign_once = pyo.Constraint(m.PERSON, rule=assign_once_rule)

    def shortage_def_rule(mm, j, s):
        attained = sum(d["skill"][p][s] * mm.x[p, j] for p in mm.PERSON)
        return mm.u[j, s] == d["required"][j][s] - attained
    m.shortage_def = pyo.Constraint(m.JS, rule=shortage_def_rule)

    def shortage_ub_rule(mm, j, s):
        return mm.u[j, s] <= d["shortage_ub"][(j, s)]
    m.shortage_ub = pyo.Constraint(m.JS, rule=shortage_ub_rule)

    def max_shortage_rule(mm, j, s):
        return mm.u[j, s] <= mm.T
    m.max_shortage = pyo.Constraint(m.JS, rule=max_shortage_rule)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=m.T, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return m
